title: First ARPANET Message
summary: On 29 October 1969 a UCLA team under Leonard Kleinrock, with student programmer Charley Kline at the keyboard, tried to log in to a computer at the Stanford Research Institute over the new ARPANET link. The system crashed after the letters "lo"; a full login worked later that night.

uncertainty.note: Day agreed by all sources; clock time is given as 10:30 p.m. by ICANN and the IEEE milestone text, but the Computer History Museum says Kline typed at around nine p.m., with the connection fully in place by 10:30 p.m.

where.modern_name: SRI International, Menlo Park, California, USA (pin is the receiving end; the message was sent from UCLA, Los Angeles)
where.historical_name: Stanford Research Institute, Menlo Park, California, United States

importance.justification: First documented host-to-host connection on ARPANET, a precursor of the Internet.

sources.title: The Computer History Museum, SRI International, and BBN Celebrate the 40th Anniversary of First ARPANET Transmission
Milestones: Inception of the ARPANET, 1969
sources.publisher: IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki

reviewer_note: Clock time conflicts (CHM ~9 p.m. vs 10:30 p.m.); pin is SRI Building A plaque GPS (proxy for receiving end), not UCLA; ETHW is a wiki-hosted IEEE page.
